$comment: Your source whitelist. Copy this file to feeds.json and edit it, or run as-is to use these examples. tier 1 = primary or trusted sources (pass the editorial gate automatically), tier 2 = broader sources held to a stricter LLM gate. weight feeds the ranking score. type: rss | discourse (a Discourse forum latest.json) | reddit (a subreddit .json listing) | listing (a scraped index page for blogs with no feed, needs linkPattern) | gnews (a Google News query feed scoped to one outlet with no usable RSS, and give every gnews feed an includePattern or Google's padding reaches the gate) | farcaster (link discovery from a channel, url 'channel:<id>', needs NEYNAR_API_KEY) | youtube (a channel's videos.xml feed) | podcast (a standard podcast RSS with audio enclosures). youtube and podcast feeds fill the podcasts shelf beside the news, never the story pipeline: tier 1 shows shelve every episode, tier 2 shows face the LLM media gate, and sectionHint is the label tier 1 episodes carry. Media-only fields: includePattern (regex a title or description must match to be considered at all, the entry ticket for a broad channel), alwaysPattern (titles matching it skip the media gate and take the feed's sectionHint, for a recurring segment that always belongs), titleRewrite ({pattern, replacement}, one case-insensitive regex pass over every title from that feed, to calm a show that shouts). sectionHint is a default section id the editor may override. category is admin-only grouping ('forum' additionally caps the importance of single-source forum stories). Admin state can disable feeds or override tier/weight/category.
